note: Each entry alpha-renames the sha256 values found at the listed keys to <ALLOWED:id#n> (first-appearance order) and renames every other occurrence of the same value (and its 16-hex prefix in generated file names) identically; non-digest scalars at the listed keys become <ALLOWED:id>. Values may differ between runs; the equality structure (which fields share a digest) must still match. Keys are bare field names or dotted key suffixes (array levels skipped). Add entries only with a written reason proven by a failing replay. WP1b adds two entry forms (introducedBy "WP1b"): `renames` ([agent-workflow literal, pi-workflow literal] pairs applied to the normalized replay before comparison; every hit is reported) and `differences` (patterns over the leaf differences of the WP1b comparison, test/replay/compare.mjs). WP1b `keys` entries are applied by the WP1b comparison only; the committed normalized/ trees stay the WP1a policy output (entries with introducedBy "WP1a").

entries.reason: sha256 of an absolute host path, or of bytes/canonical JSON that embed absolute host paths (generated worker extension wrapper and its config embed manifestPath/ledgerPath/runDir; tool-provider descriptors embed extension paths). The paths themselves are normalized to <ROOT>/<PKG>/<HOME>/<TMP> and compared; their digests cannot be.

Digest of the private workflow state root identity (src/workflow-state-root.ts): canonical path, device, inode, uid, mode and a random per-root nonce file. Host- and install-specific by design; cannot be reproduced in another directory.

Canonical self-digests of launch provenance records that include host-path-digest and state-root-identity values (launch bootstrap provenance identity, launch authority grant identity) and every field that references them (launchBootstrapSha256, launchAuthoritySha256, durable barrier subjectSha256, generated .launch-barrier-<16hex> directory prefix).
Raw-artifact owner identity is sha256 over JSON that includes the workflow run createdAt timestamp (src/workflow-raw-contract.ts). Timestamps are normalized to <TS>; a digest over one cannot be.

terminalVersion.size is the byte size of the pi-subagent attempt result.json, a file that embeds absolute host paths (cwd, artifactCwd); its length changes with the project path length. dev/ino/mtimeMs/ctimeMs of the same stamp are already policy placeholders.

Digests of the task's source-manifest.json, whose artifact entries embed absolute <ROOT> paths, so the values change with the project path: launchBootstrap records[].artifacts.manifestSha256 = sha256 over its canonical JSON and effectiveLaunch.artifactBinding.manifestBytesSha256 = sha256 over its bytes (src/launch-bootstrap-provenance.ts). They occur only for stages with upstream artifact access (first seen in fixtures/deep-review task-7; minimal's manifest has no paths, so its digest happened to match). Content stays pinned: the manifest file itself is compared after path normalization, the self-replay test asserts both replayed digests equal the digests of the replayed source-manifest.json, and the fixture build verified the same binding on the raw recording.

Profile-only foreach batching (deep-research low/medium verify-claims, max 2 items) records run.json foreachBatches[] with stateRootSha256 (the same host-specific state-root identity as effectivePolicy.stateRootSha256, so its run.json occurrences are already renamed by equality) and capabilitySubjectSha256 = sha256 over canonical JSON of the batch record including that stateRootSha256 and the preparedAt timestamp (src/foreach-batch-capability.ts). The engine also passes both values to durableLaunchBarrierDigest (reservation payload schema workflow-foreach-batch-dispatch-reservation-v1), where no effectivePolicy key renames the state root inside that single call's replay key. The prompt content stays compared: foreachBatches[].batchPromptSha256 and members[].preparedPromptSha256 are not masked.

supervisor.json is the supervisor heartbeat file; taskStatusCounts is the progress snapshot taken at its last write (src/store.ts run progress), which races the final task transitions. Observed in fixtures/deep-research: recording completed=20/pending=1, replay completed=19 in 3 of 3 replays (the minimal, deep-review, spec-review and impact-review fixtures happened to match). Final per-task statuses stay compared through run.json tasks[] and taskSummary; taskStatusCounts.total is not masked.

entries.decision: WP4b env/path renames (docs/core-port.md "WP4b env / path renames", change log 1) and WP4c-1 literal renames (docs/core-port.md "Paths, env and literals", change log 10)
entries.reason: agent-workflow writes the same records under renamed paths and identifiers: run state under .agent-workflow/workflows instead of .pi/workflows, runtime runs under .agent-workflow/workflow-subagents, worker session ids agent-workflow.<run>.<task> instead of pi-workflow.<run>.<task> (they are also part of the launch attempt identity string), the task backend id agent-workflow/runtime instead of pi-subagent/headless, and the worker system prompt opening 'You are workflow subagent' instead of 'You are Pi workflow subagent'. The replay is renamed back literal by literal after normalization; each hit is listed in the report. Digests over renamed text are not masked by this entry.

entries.decision: WP10 worker prompt rendering (docs/core-port.md "WP10" change log 1, docs/bundled-workflows.md): the task backend renders the logical tool name workflow_artifact to the executor's visible name artifactToolVisibleName(executorId) in the task and system prompts
entries.reason: The replay registers its executor as "pi", whose MCP client shows the artifact tool as mcp__workflow_artifact__workflow_artifact (verified live, docs/executors/pi.md #4). pi-workflow's Pi extension registered the tool under the bare name workflow_artifact. Every tool mention in task.md, system-prompt.md and the launch prompt is renamed back literal by literal; each hit is listed in the report. Evidence locators (workflow_artifact:<id>) are never rendered.

entries.decision: WP12a control schema path in executor prompts (docs/core-port.md "WP12a" change log 4)
entries.reason: The compiled output protocol names the control schema relative to the workflow bundle (./schemas/<file>), which does not resolve from the worker's cwd (live bundle 3 open problem 3). The task backend renders the run's own copy (<run>/bundle/schemas/<file>, absolute) into the prompt sent to the executor; task.md keeps the compiled text. The launch prompt is renamed back literal by literal for the replay match key; each hit is listed in the report.

entries.decision: 2026-10-30 owner decision: agent-workflow no longer reads Pi's directories (~/.pi/agent, a project's .pi); docs/usage.md "Agents"
entries.reason: The recordings ran with their agents in <project>/.pi/agents; agent-workflow reads project agents only from <project>/.agent-workflow/agents, so the replay driver installs the same agent files there. Agent paths in compiled.json/run.json name that directory instead; the agent bytes are unchanged.

entries.decision: WP4c-1 literal rename: usage/budget record source "pi-subagent" → "executor" (docs/core-port.md "Paths, env and literals")
entries.reason: Task usage and per-attempt timing records name their source "executor" (any executor) instead of "pi-subagent". A bare-word rename of "executor" would be too broad, so only these two keys are allowed to differ, and only with exactly these values.

entries.decision: WP2a-2/WP4c-1: the durable launch barrier is created by the in-repo runtime (docs/runtime-port.md "Durable LaunchAuthority", docs/core-port.md policy row 13) instead of being echoed from the recording
entries.reason: The WP1a self-replay served the recorded barrier descriptor, so its random challenge and decisionNonce (randomBytes per launch) and every digest over them came back verbatim. The WP1b replay runs the real runtime barrier, which draws fresh nonces and binds them with runtime ids, timestamps, the executor descriptor and the worker payload bytes: barrier identity (descriptor.identitySha256 / barrierIdentitySha256), READY/decision/ACK file digests, the release payload digest, the launch payload digest (sha256 of worker.json, which holds runtime run/attempt ids and startedAt) and the execution plan digest (runtime run/attempt ids, cwd, descriptor and the SubmitRequest). These are self-digests of one launch; the alpha-renaming still requires the same equality structure between run.json and the barrier files. Prompt content is not masked by this entry: task.md, launchBootstrap prompt.sha256/bytes and the replay match key are compared exactly. A foreach batch dispatch reservation (foreachBatches[].dispatch.reservationSha256) digests the release payload digest, so it follows it.

entries.decision: WP4b run state path rename .pi/workflows → .agent-workflow/workflows (docs/core-port.md WP4b change log 1) and the WP4c-1 literal renames (change log 10), seen through digests
entries.reason: Some records digest bytes that contain a renamed literal: a task source-manifest.json lists its upstream artifacts by absolute path under the run state directory, and the original spec-review helper quotes the manifest's sha256 (candidateManifestSha256) in its control, whose own digest field then reaches the next task's prompt. The renamed literal changes those digests although nothing else differs. A replayed digest is replaced by the recorded one only with a binding check (test/replay/digest-binding.mjs): `file` — both digests are recomputed from the two files (recorded bytes with the recorded host root restored) and the files are equal after normalization, the literal renames and the bindings proven before; `self` — a JSON control whose `digest` is sha256 over stableStringify(rest) on both sides and whose rest is equal after the same steps. Only fixtures that pin the recorded root (replayRoot) can be checked. Every binding is listed in the report with its proof file. Prompt, output and manifest contents are never masked: they still compare exactly after the substitution.

entries.decision: WP4b run state path rename (docs/core-port.md WP4b change log 1) inside a digest the record does not let us recompute
entries.reason: foreachBatches[].executionSurfaceSha256 is sha256 over the canonical prepared leader task (cwd, agent, runtime, safety, artifactGraph — foreach-batch-runtime.ts foreachBatchExecutionSurfaceSha256). The prepared artifactGraph names run-state paths under the renamed .agent-workflow/workflows; compiled.json, which holds the same compiled fields, compares equal after the literal renames. The prepared task itself is not recorded, so no binding check is possible; the entry is limited to this one key, the equality structure (all batches of one stage share one surface) must still match, and the batch prompts, receipts and outputs are compared exactly.
